subject: Structured credits vs upfront commit — GPU stack choice
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@apollo-analytics.com>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool pricing — credits vs commit?

Rafael,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we scope a dedicated pool for our inference workload (multi-model):

- Target sustained throughput: ~100 qps for chat models (avg payload ~400 tokens), with predictable peaks up to 600 qps for short windows.
- Tail latency target: 95th <= 120ms for chat endpoints.
- Mixed workload: half the requests are high-context (requiring 80GB+ KV cache), the rest are shorter embeddings/classification ops.
- North America deployment, need SOC2 evidence and auditability.

Two commercial questions:
1) We want a pricing comparison: structured credits (monthly/yearly credits we draw down) vs a traditional upfront reserved commit (12–24 months). How do discounts, unused-credit rollovers, and termination flex look?
2) On the GPU mix: our engineers are debating A100 80GB vs H100 vs L40S. For our profile (mixed long-context + high qps bursts), what perf/$ tradeoffs should we expect and what would you recommend for a first-year commit?

Can you share a ballpark proposal (preferred: numeric anchors) so we can take to procurement? We can send detailed telemetry if helpful — attaching a small sample payload profile.

Thanks,
Samir

Samir — appreciate the detailed profile. High level first, then we can follow with a formal term sheet and a short call (30 min) to lock assumptions.

Quick answers / anchors:
- Two commercial paths we commonly propose:
  1) Structured credits: monthly or quarterly credits you buy in advance. Credits roll forward for one quarter; unused after the rollover window are forfeited. This gives flexibility (no vesting) and a modest discount vs PAYG (~15–22% depending on term and volume).
  2) Upfront reserved commit (12–24 months): larger discounts in exchange for usage commit. Typical anchors: 20–35% off hosted pay-as-you-go for a 12-mo commit; 30–45% for 24-mo plus larger minimums. We can layer in service credits or guaranteed throughput SLAs for committed customers.

- Unused credits / termination: structured credits are cancellable at quarter boundaries; reserved commits have early-termination fees but can be partially reallocated to other projects within your org. We can discuss a phased release schedule for the first 90 days if you want flexibility.

- GPU mix (ballpark recommendation for your profile):
  * H100 (latency-first, high perf/$ for short sequences): use for endpoints where you need bursty, low-latency responses. H100 gives best perf for transformer kernels and lower latency at higher concurrency.
  * A100 80GB (long-context, KV-heavy models): preferable for >4k token working sets and large KV caches; more memory reduces model-slicing and avoids offloading. Perf/$ for long contexts is competitive but you pay for the large memory buckets.
  * L40S (cost-effective, dense inference): good for embeddings and lower-precision workloads where memory footprint is smaller; excellent perf/$ on throughput but not ideal for the 80GB KV use-case.

Suggested starter allocation for a 12-mo commit (example):
  - 40% H100 (burst and chat endpoints)
  - 40% A100 80GB (long-context models)
  - 20% L40S (embeddings, batch jobs)

Marcus — I’m looping you and Vanessa in to sketch a concrete pricing anchor (commit size and percent discounts) so we can send Samir a short term sheet (PDF). Samir — would you be open to a quick call Thursday 12/3 at 10am PT to walk the numbers?

Best,

Subject: FW: Dedicated pool pricing — quick pricing model (internal)

Rafa / Vanessa — internal sketch for Apollo based on the profile Rafael shared. Raw numbers to convert into the term sheet:

Assumptions:
- Sustained baseline: 100 qps = ~3.2B tokens/month (estimate from their sample).
- Peak buffer capacity: need headroom for 3x bursts (600 qps).
- Model mix: 55% chat (low-latency), 30% long-context, 15% embeddings/batch.

Option A: Structured credits (annualized equivalent)
- Monthly credits purchased = baseline * 1.2 (to cover bursts) => commit-equivalent $X = $200k/month (example anchor).
- Discount vs PAYG: 18% for 12-mo prepay, 22% for 24-mo prepay.
- Roll-forward: one quarter. No early termination fee.

Option B: Upfront reserved commit (12 months)
- Commit size: $180k/month baseline with 15% true-up flexibility
- Discounts: 28% (12-mo) / 38% (24-mo) off PAYG depending on GPU mix and minimums.
- SLA: 99.5% uptime with throughput SLO for routed endpoints; 12-hour response for major incidents.
- Early termination: pro-rated remaining unused commit + 10% fee (negotiable for enterprise).

GPU mix pricing impact (monthly cost delta vs all-H100 baseline):
- Mixed 40/40/20 (H100/A100/L40S): ~ -14% cost vs all-H100 baseline, with improved 95p latency on long-context ops.
- Heavier A100 tilt (30/50/20): ~ +6% cost compared to mixed, but reduces long-context token failure/retry by ~60%. Good if their long-context models are business-critical.
- L40S-heavy (50% L40S): ~ -28% cost but expect latency and context limitations.

Recommendations to propose in term sheet:
1) Start with 12-mo reserved commit at $180k/mo with a 30% blended discount and a 90-day phased deployment to validate perf assumptions.
2) Include a structured-credit addendum to allow up to 20% of monthly volume to be handled via credits for the first 6 months (gives Apollo runout flexibility).
3) If Apollo signs for 24 months and increases commit by +30%, we can escalate to 40% discount and commit to H100 priority routing during US peak windows.

I’ll drop a short term-sheet PDF and a benchmark CSV (H100/A100/L40S perf per model size) for Rafael to send. Numbers above are anchors — we should be explicit in the email to procurement that these are negotiable and depend on the final model mix telemetry.

-Marcus
Director, Pricing & Economics

Samir — attaching a short term sheet and the benchmark CSV we discussed. Key points in short:

- Offer (12-month reserved commit): $180,000 / month commit (APL-2026-98) => blended ~30% discount vs PAYG; includes 90-day phased onboarding and an initial model calibration window.
- Structured-credit addendum: up to 20% of monthly volume may be run on a monthly prepay credit that rolls one quarter; credits priced at ~18% below PAYG. This provides runout flexibility for your unpredictable bursts during early deployment.
- Recommended GPU mix (initial): 40% H100 / 40% A100 80GB / 20% L40S. We can re-evaluate at month 3 with telemetry and adjust allocation without changing the commit price (capacity reallocation permitted within defined limits).
- Attachments: redwood_commit_term_sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet with sample SLA clauses and PO instructions), example-benchmark-a100-h100-l40s.csv (per-model latency & throughput anchors).

Next steps:
1) Let me know if procurement wants any contract language edits; we can provide a redline-friendly version.
2) If this looks reasonable, confirm and I’ll route to Legal for a draft MSA.
3) Proposed kickoff: onboarding week starting 2027-01-04.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a call if you want to walk the numbers.

Best,
